ns2:section.sectionText: Genomic Biology This course will explore genomic and genetic resources that are available to enrich and accelerate modern biological research. Lectures will focus on the methods used to generate these resources and their applications, supported by reading of the relevant primary research literature. In-class exercises and assignments will explore databases, web-based tools, and analytical software available for users to exploit public data for practical research use. The first portion of the course will focus on genome sequence annotation, using in silico and in vitro methods; comparative genomics; and genome evolution. The second portion will explore resources and methods for in vivo analysis of gene and non-coding DNA function and interactions. The discussion will emphasize human, mouse and other well-characterized genomes, but illustrate approaches with application to a wide variety of other eukaryotic model systems. This class will meet in 607 IGB.
